newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher, caution prevails.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher, caution prevails.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed higher Tuesday, cheered by the two-day rebound on Wall Street and the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to keep rates steady.
"The market here is doing well, although it's still undermined by the volatility we saw even today on Wall Street," said Gabriel Ruiz at brokers Tavelli.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV jumped 1.3 percent to 850.01, recouping most of the losses incurred last week.
"If things calm down abroad the bolsa might finally embark on a steady upward course, because local fundamentals remain very solid," Tavelli said.

He also said the Argentine bolsa had an edge over other emerging markets. "It's lagging the main Latin American bourses as far as this year's gains are concerned, and of course there's turbulence in Asia," he said.

Traders noted even though the bolsa got off to a late start ahead of the Fed's announcement on rates, floor volume remained healthy at 33.3 million pesos against 34.8 million Friday (Monday was a holiday). Over-the-counter turnover surged to 155.1 million pesos from 48.3 million Friday.
"Institutional investors are pretty active here and keeping the undertone firm," another dealer said.
The broad market index inched up 0.2 percent, with winners outpacing losers 25 to 17 and 27 issues closing unchanged.

Top blue-chip gainers were steelmakers Siderca and Siderar, which rallied 4.6 percent and 3.8 percent, respectively, carmaker Sevel, up 4.5 percent, and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, up 3.1 percent.
MerVal losers were led by foods giant Molinos, cement stock Polledo and oil company Astra, off 3.4 percent, 2.4 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively.
